text: Arthur the rat. Once there was a young rat named Arthur who could never make up his mind. Whenever his friends asked him if he would like to go out with them, he would only answer, I don't know. He wouldn't say yes or no either. He would always ship making a choice. His aunt Helen said to him, now look here, no one is going to take care for you if you carry on like this. You have no more mind than a blade of grass. One rainy day the rats heard a great noise in the loft. The pine rafters were all rotten, so that the barn was rather unsafe. At last the joists gave way and fell to the ground. The walls shook and all the rats' heads stood on end with fear and horror. This won't do, said the captain. I will send out scouts to search for a new home. Within five hours, the tent scouts came back and said, �We have found a stone house where there is room and board for us all. There is a kindly horse named Nelly, a cow, a calf and a garden with an elm tree.� The rats crawled out of their little houses and stood on the floor in a long line. just then the old one saw arthur stop he ordered coarsely you're coming of course i'm not certain said arthur undaunted the roof may not come down yet Well, said the angry old rat. We can't wait for you to join us. Right about face, march. Arthur stood and watched them hurry away. I think I will go tomorrow, he calmly said to himself. But then again, I don't know. It's so nice and snug here. That night, there was a big crash. In the morning, some men with some boys and girls rode up and looked at the barn. One of them moved a board, and he saw a young rat, quite dead, half in and half out of its hole. Thus the shrieker got his due.
